text:
Max H: Heads up — seeing a sharp east-west latency spike in us-west-2 during the 09:15-09:25 batch window. p95 gpu->gpu jumped from ~12ms to ~180ms, and some token queues started backing up. Observed ~0.5-1% packet loss between 10.0.4.x <-> 10.0.5.x.
Anya S: Copy. Affected pool? RDMA nodes? any recent config changes?
Max H: Affected pool is batch-a-west (RDMA-enabled A100). Kernel 5.15. We had an infra config push at ~03:00 that touched NIC settings and a SwitchController update around the same time.
Miguel R: Can you paste the interface stats + MTU on two adjacent nodes? suspect MTU or offload mismatch.
Max H: Paste below (node-a vs node-b):
```
node-a# ip -s link show ens1f0
2: ens1f0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 123456789 packets 987654 errors 0 dropped 3 overruns 0
    TX: bytes 987654321 packets 876543 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0

node-b# ip -s link show ens1f0
2: ens1f0: mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 22334455 packets 192837 errors 0 dropped 120 overruns 0
    TX: bytes 55667788 packets 334455 errors 0 dropped 2 overruns 0
```
Max H: So node-b shows MTU=1500 and ~120 RX drops in the window.
Shweta (netops): That MTU mismatch will do it for jumbo traffic. Also odd drops on RX. Were any ONOS/switch rules rolled out?
infra-bot: SwitchController: applied update 03:02 UTC -> rewrote L2 config on spine-02 (change id sc-2026-03). No rollback recorded.
Anya S: If RDMA path expects 9k and one side is 1500, you get fragmentation or drops. Try toggling GRO/GSO/TSO on the interface as a quick test.
Miguel R: Agreed. Quick canary: disable GRO/GSO/TSO on node-b and re-run a short batch test.
Max H: Running on node-b now:
```
sudo ethtool -K ens1f0 gro off gso off tso off
# re-run micro-batch test
# obs p95 -> 14ms, packet drops -> 0 in next 2 min
```
Max H: Immediate improvement after disabling offloads. Looks like jumbo mismatch + offload interaction.
Shweta (netops): OK that's a useful mitigation. Two action items: 1) roll the MTU to 9000 consistently across batch-a-west (switch + host), 2) audit the SwitchController change that touched MTU or L2 configs and add a guard for host MTU drift.
Anya S: Also add an agent check in node bootstrap to assert MTU==expected for RDMA pools; fail fast before joining.
Miguel R: For short-term: we'll keep GRO/GSO/TSO off on the impacted nodes and add a daemon to restore offloads only after MTU reconciliation.
Max H: I'm patching a flipper script to disable offloads on rollout and adding a prom metric 'net.mtu_mismatch' to alert before the next peak window.
Shweta (netops): I'll open a ticket to roll spine-02 change back or patch its config by EOD. Need a maintenance window to safely reconfigure MTU on all hosts. Suggest midday low-traffic window and drain nodes via scheduler.
Anya S: Who's owning the change? Miguel/Max can coordinate host side, Shweta owns switch side. I'll own the presubmit that checks MTU in the infra CI.
Miguel R: I'll schedule a rolling reconfigure for the pool: drain -> set MTU 9000 -> re-enable offloads -> smoke test. ETA tomorrow 12:30 PST. Will post runbook here.
Max H: Thanks everyone. For now, we've mitigated the current spike by disabling offloads; telemetry shows p95 back to normal and no queueing. Will follow up with postmortem and runbook.
Shweta (netops): Great. Assigning incident tag and priority P2. Please add short postmortem and link to runbook when done. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-239 (east-west mtu mismatch during batch window)"
